mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between HOUST declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
